S-001.threat: OT protocol sender spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate OT device
S-001.cause: OT protocol stack carries no sender authentication
S-001.attack: Attacker connects a rogue device to the OT network and impersonates a legitimate PLC or sensor

S-002.threat: Embedded system identity spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate embedded controller or safety system
S-002.cause: No hardware-based authentication between embedded systems — systemClass identity is not verified
S-002.attack: Attacker places a rogue embedded device claiming to be a legitimate controller and injects falsified commands

S-003.threat: Sensor spoofing — an attacker impersonates the sensor or injects forged readings from a rogue device
S-003.cause: Sensor identity and readings are not authenticated
S-003.attack: Attacker feeds forged measurements from a rogue or cloned sensor

S-004.threat: Command spoofing — an attacker issues commands that appear to come from an authorized controller
S-004.cause: The command source is not authenticated
S-004.attack: Attacker sends forged actuation commands on the control channel
